title: Default `JAVA_HOME` overrides valid system Java with a machine-specific path
reasoning: When `JAVA_HOME` is unset, the Makefile forces Gradle to use a hardcoded Android Studio JBR path. On machines or CI runners with Java available through PATH or another installed JDK but without Android Studio at exactly this location, Gradle will receive an invalid `JAVA_HOME` and fail before the wrapper can use the otherwise valid Java installation.
reproduction: Run `env -u JAVA_HOME make -n xcframework`; the Gradle command expands with `JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home"`.
recommendation: Do not set a machine-specific `JAVA_HOME` by default. Prefer inheriting the environment/PATH, or conditionally choose this Android Studio JBR only when the directory exists, with a clear error if no usable Java is found.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or CI job exercise the Makefile with `JAVA_HOME` unset on a clean machine image.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI smoke test that runs the Makefile with `JAVA_HOME` unset on the supported runner image and verifies the Gradle wrapper starts successfully.
minimumFixScope: Change the `JAVA_HOME`/`GRADLE` definitions in `Makefile` to avoid forcing a non-portable default.
